traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 100 records annotated as flowering (Apr 57, May 38, Jun 4, Jul 1); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, April and May. The Seed Manual (Amelanchier chapter, printed p. 246) gives April at 520 m and May at 1,310 m in Oregon (var. semiintegrifolia).

traits.fruiting_months.note: Seed Manual, Amelanchier chapter (printed p. 246): ripe in August at 520 m in Oregon (var. semiintegrifolia, the Pacific serviceberry). FEIS gives July to September across the range. Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 68: fruit ripe June-July. Not combined: Dendrology's months are for the tree grown in Europe, the spec's for its own range.

traits.height_max_m.note: Jepson (1925), as A. alnifolia: grows 91 cm to 3.66 m tall (converted from feet).

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an upright shrub of slender grey stems with round leaves toothed only near the tip and sprays of white flowers with narrow petals. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 3.2 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: blue-green rounded leaves; white flowers; smooth grey bark. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: racemes of purple berries crowned by the calyx, a third still red. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: white flowers in April and May; berries purple in late June and July. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth grey bark; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): white strap-shaped petals 9 to 14 mm long round about 20 stamens, in short racemes that open from the base up. From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five white petals between five sepals on a floral cup joined to the inferior ovary, twenty stamens and a pistil of five carpels, from the characters of Rosaceae and Amelanchier by the rules at the flowering plants.

appearance.organs.bloom.season.opening.note: Days from the first flower of a cluster opening to its last: a third of the days from its first flower to its first fruit as they were set by hand before 2026-10-14, a convention (no source gives a raceme's opening time).

traits.inflorescence.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 68, Amelanchier alnifolia: inflorescence raceme, erect, 2-4(-6) cm, 5-11(-15) flowers.

traits.fruit_type.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 68, Amelanchier alnifolia: fruit type pome, dark purple-black, 1-1.5 cm.
